model_annotation: The image displays a donut chart with two concentric rings, representing two different metrics: "Ambiguity Std (Outer)" in the outer ring and "Max Ambiguity (Inner)" in the inner ring. The outer ring is divided into four segments, each corresponding to a standard deviation value (Std: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), with colors ranging from dark blue to light blue, and labeled with percentages: 49.0%, 39.0%, 7.0%, and 5.0% respectively. The inner ring is divided into three segments, corresponding to maximum ambiguity values (Max: 1, 2, 3), shown in varying shades of light blue, with percentages labeled as 47.7%, 38.0%, and 14.2%. The chart includes two legends on the right side: the upper legend for the outer ring maps the four standard deviation values to their respective colors, and the lower legend for the inner ring maps the three maximum ambiguity values to their colors. The segments in both rings appear to be arranged in descending order of percentage size, starting from the top-right and proceeding clockwise. The chart visually compares the distribution of ambiguity metrics across different standard deviation and maximum ambiguity categories.
